decisive_transcriptions.transcription:
Report No. 5936
DDN COMPARATIVE COST ANALYSIS
James A. Kane, Peter J. Sevcik, and Gary H. Tauss
Contract No. DCA200-84-C-0017
Task Order 4-2A
April 1985
Prepared for:
Defense Communications Agency
This document describes an analytical method to compare the costs of the Defense Data Network, public data networks, and private dedicated networks for wide-area data communications.

A case study of the Marine Corps Data Network is presented using the analysis framework. The case study shows that DDN is the least expensive alternative and that discretionary costs are a significant portion of total costs.
decisive_transcriptions.status: visually checked; claim is the authors’ summary, not an independently audited result

decisive_transcriptions.transcription: The original program plan called for the DDN to be financed eventually by subscribers through a usage-based cost recovery system.
decisive_transcriptions.status: visually checked; program plan not dated here

decisive_transcriptions.transcription: The analytical framework presented in this section assumes that a current or prospective DDN subscriber wishes to compare DDN subscriber usage charges (were the hypothetical DDN tariff in effect) to the costs of comparable service from a public data network or a private dedicated network.

We recognize that it is unrealistic to think that some users actually could use network alternatives other than DDN because of current DoD policy and other considerations. Nevertheless, the analytical method provides for these alternatives in order to have a means of comparing subscriber costs of the hypothetical DDN tariff to actual costs and charges that a user would incur today for other network alternatives.
The cost comparison methodology includes three network alternatives to fulfill subscribers’ data communication requirements: DDN, a public data network, and a dedicated private network.
